title: Fit a Multi-Seasonal ARIMA Model — msarima
text: y numeric vector time series object (ts msts) containing data modelled. y ts object seasonal.period supplied, frequency used first seasonal period; y msts object, seasonal periods used. order numeric vector length 3 specifying non-seasonal part ARIMA model: AR order (p), degree differencing (d), MA order (q). Default c(0, 0, 0). seasonal list numeric vectors, length 3, specifying seasonal components. vector gives seasonal AR order (P), seasonal differencing order (D), seasonal MA order (Q) one component. example, list(c(1, 0, 1), c(0, 1, 1)) specifies two seasonal components. Use list() model without seasonal components. Default list(). seasonal.period numeric vector seasonal periods, one element seasonal, example c(7, 30) weekly monthly seasonality. NULL, periods taken y ts msts object. Default NULL. fixed numeric vector one entry per parameter, used hold given value: NA entries estimated. parameters ordered non-seasonal AR, seasonal AR (one block per seasonal component), non-seasonal MA, seasonal MA (one block per seasonal component), sigma, constant term include.constant = TRUE. Default NULL, meaning parameters estimated. include.constant model include constant term? constant intercept model equation, mean series: stationary model two related mean = intercept / prod(1 - ar). constant combined differencing dropped, warning, d D non-zero. Default FALSE. optim_control list control parameters passed optim. Default list(maxit = 200).

title: Fit a Multi-Seasonal ARIMA Model — msarima
text: object class "msarima", list containing: order non-seasonal ARIMA order (p, d, q). seasonal List seasonal component specifications. seasonal.period Vector seasonal periods. coef Named vector estimated coefficients: AR, SAR, MA SMA parameters, followed intercept include.constant = TRUE. var_coef Variance-covariance matrix coefficient estimates. mask Logical vector indicating parameters fixed. loglik Log-likelihood fitted model. aic Akaike Information Criterion. bic Bayesian Information Criterion. aicc Corrected Akaike Information Criterion. sigma2 Estimated innovation variance. x original time series. fitted One-step-ahead fitted values, scale original series. residuals Model residuals. Together fitted, first d + sum(D * S) values NA, since differencing leaves observation predict . method Description fitted model. series Name series. nobs Number observations original series. n.used Number observations used estimation (differencing). call matched call. convergence Convergence code optim (0 indicates successful convergence).

title: Fit a Multi-Seasonal ARIMA Model — msarima
text: model estimated conditional maximum likelihood: residuals computed recursively resulting Gaussian log-likelihood maximised numerically optim, using BFGS algorithm. d D non-zero, series differenced estimation ARMA part estimated differenced data. first d + sum(D * S) observations therefore used, residuals start many NA values. Standard errors computed inverse observed information matrix (negative Hessian). Hessian singular, warning issued standard errors set NA.

title: Fit a Multi-Seasonal ARIMA Model — msarima
text: series must least 10 observations, differencing. Seasonal periods must least 2 half length series. y ts msts object, x, fitted residuals keep time series structure. y plain numeric vector, returned ts one seasonal period, msts several.

title: Fit a Multi-Seasonal ARIMA Model — msarima
code: # Example 1: ARIMA with two seasonal components set.seed(123) y <- msarima.sim(nsim = 200,                  order = c(1, 0, 0),                  seasonal = list(c(1, 0, 0), c(0, 0, 1)),                  seasonal.period = c(4, 11),                  ar = c(0.5, 0.5), ma = 0.3, sigma2 = 1)  fit <- msarima(y, order = c(1, 0, 0),                seasonal = list(c(1, 0, 0), c(0, 0, 1)),                seasonal.period = c(4, 11)) print(fit) #> Series: y  #> MSARIMA(1,0,0)(1,0,0)[4](0,0,1)[11] #>  #> Coefficients: #>    AR(1) SAR(1,1) SMA(2,1)  #>   0.4101   0.4678   0.3805  #>  #> sigma^2 = 0.9272  log likelihood = -92.44 #> AIC = 192.88   AICc = 193.08   BIC = 206.07 summary(fit) #> Series: y  #> MSARIMA(1,0,0)(1,0,0)[4](0,0,1)[11] #>  #> Coefficients: #>          Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)     #> AR(1)     0.41006    0.06570   6.241 4.35e-10 *** #> SAR(1,1)  0.46782    0.06428   7.278 3.40e-13 *** #> SMA(2,1)  0.38051    0.06943   5.481 4.24e-08 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> sigma^2 = 0.9272  log likelihood = -92.4387 #> AIC = 192.8775   AICc = 193.0826   BIC = 206.0707  # Example 2: msts input, seasonal periods detected automatically y_msts <- msts(y, seasonal.periods = c(4, 11)) fit_msts <- msarima(y_msts, order = c(1, 0, 0),                     seasonal = list(c(1, 0, 0), c(0, 0, 1)))  # Example 3: differencing fit_diff <- msarima(cumsum(y), order = c(1, 1, 0),                     seasonal = list(c(0, 0, 1)),                     seasonal.period = 4) head(residuals(fit_diff))  # the first residual is NA #>         Qtr1       Qtr2       Qtr3       Qtr4 #> 1         NA -0.7053174 -2.4672228 -0.1094124 #> 2  0.4100991 -2.0204887                        # Example 4: fixing parameters # Note: the length of 'fixed' must match AR + SAR + MA + SMA + sigma fit_fixed <- msarima(y, order = c(1, 0, 0),                      seasonal = list(c(1, 0, 0), c(0, 0, 1)),                      seasonal.period = c(4, 11),                      fixed = c(0.5, NA, NA, NA)) AIC(fit); AIC(fit_fixed) #> [1] 192.8775 #> [1] 192.7455

Use list() model without seasonal components. Default list(). seasonal.period numeric vector seasonal periods, one element seasonal. Default NULL. ar Numeric vector AR coefficients, non-seasonal first one block per seasonal component. length must match total AR order implied order seasonal. Default NULL. ma Numeric vector MA coefficients, ordered ar. length must match total MA order implied order seasonal. Default NULL. sigma2 Innovation variance. Default 1. burn Number burn-observations discard. NULL, set max(100, 2 * kk), kk largest lag model. Default NULL. intercept Constant term model equation, \(\mu\) \(y_t = \mu + \sum \phi_i y_{t-} + \sum \theta_j e_{t-j} + e_t\). intercept, mean process: stationary model mean intercept / prod(1 - ar). Default 0.

title: msarima 0.0.0.9006
text: New sacf() spacf(), autocorrelation partial autocorrelation plots highlight lags seasonal cycle, periods taken msts object fitted model. ggsacf() ggspacf() ggplot2 versions. New vignette msarima, walk-package MAD_m40. New dataset MAD_m40: hourly traffic volume M-40 ring road Madrid, February May 2024, msts object seasonal periods 24 168. Fixed estimation models differencing msarima(). differencing operator folded AR polynomial conditional sum squares computed undifferenced series, padded constant. first d + sum(D * S) residuals therefore start-transient (entered likelihood biased estimates), residuals() length input series. series now differenced estimation, fitting msarima(x, order = c(p, 0, q), seasonal = list(c(0, 1, 1))) gives exactly coefficients residuals fitting ARMA diff(x, S). residuals() fitted() now NA first d + sum(D * S) observations (fitted values remain scale original series). forecast.msarima() simulate.msarima() now use intercept term models fitted include.constant = TRUE. estimated never read, point forecasts decayed 0 instead mean process, simulated series centred 0. Fixed seasonal AR/MA polynomial construction forecast.msarima() (seasonal orders >= 2 placed coefficients lags S, S+1, ... instead S, 2S, ...) seasonal differencing D >= 2. fix already applied msarima() msarima.sim(). New intercept argument msarima.sim(). Fixed order greater 1 msarima() Fixed bug extract hessian msarima() Fixed seasonal AR/MA polynomial construction msarima() msarima.sim() seasonal orders >= 2. Fixed seasonal AR/MA polynomial construction (seasonal differencing D >= 2) msarima() msarima.sim(). Initial CRAN submission.
